text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.
-Saving Bank Union Bank of Norway, Danish insurer Codan and Fokus Bank may want to start a joint insurance company.
-A total of 110 persons now living in Norway may be expelled because they lied about their identity when applying for residence permits.

-Almost 70 percent of young couples in northern Norway who live together are not married. Researcher say the decision by young couples in the norht not to get married show that people there are independent-minded and have with a tradition of protesting against accepted moral standards and values in society.

-Police fear the motorcycle gang war will be stepped up and will increase efforts to crack down on the groups. After a bomb destroyed the headquarter of one of Norway's leading bike gangs last week, police say acts of reveng are likely to happen.

-Erik Toenseth, manager of Anglo-Norwegian shipbuilder and constructor group Kvaerner, says Kvaerner will probably be listed in Asia within a year. One year after buying Britain's Trafalgar House, Toenseth is pleased with the development of the company but he still thinks the share price is too low.
-Orkla-owned Borregaard will build a plant for lignosofonate together with a national company in South Africa. It will be the first time for an Orkla company to establish a unit in South Africa.
